overview: This sortie is the actual familiarization solo. The goal of these notes is to make the day-of ODO/FDO brief a confirmation brief: show up already understanding the rear-cockpit solo setup, the current weather and runway limits, the authorized profile, the emergency support plan, and when to stop training and recover.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: Treat the solo brief as the final go/no-go gate, not the first time you organize the sortie. These notes should let you walk in already understanding the major risk, weather, profile, and emergency decisions so the day-of ODO/FDO brief can confirm the current rules instead of teaching them from scratch.

children.text: Show up with rear-cockpit securing, unauthorized solo maneuvers, unintentional instrument flight, lost-aircraft logic, and support-agency call expectations already current.
Be ready to confirm the current weather minimums, runway and crosswind limits, launch and recovery windows, authorized operating areas, landing limits, and any bird or field-condition restrictions.
Know what you will do if you divert, full stop away from home field, lose radios, encounter weather you cannot remain VFR in, or find a maintenance discrepancy after landing.
Fly a conservative profile, keep fuel and time tracked, and discontinue the training objective early if the sortie stops matching the brief.
Use the current published procedure and day-of brief for the local details instead of relying on memory, old gouge, or another student's route names.
The day-of ODO/FDO solo brief still remains required even if these notes already make the picture familiar.

studyNotes.summary: Use these notes to arrive at the solo brief already clear on the go/no-go boundaries, support plan, and conservative decisions that protect a first solo.

title: Familiarization Solo Flight
